CONTENT WITH GUTENBERG AND ACF Read list-content before creating anything, then get-content before an edit. Read get-skill-doc {id:"block-discovery-contract"} before choosing or modifying a block. SAVE MODES save-content requires mode. create makes a draft; omit contentId. add appends blocks to an existing contentId; do not send the entire body when intending one insertion. replace replaces the complete body. edit applies edits to an existing contentId; supply expectedHash from the latest get-content. Use the tool's current edit schema for indexes, paths and operation arguments. A stale hash means reread, merge and retry; do not remove the hash to overwrite concurrent edits. Omitted unrelated content stays. New records are drafts; updating content preserves publication status. Publishing is a separate set-content-status operation requiring the user's intent. An HTTP success is not a visual verification. REGISTERED BLOCKS / ACF New or changed blocks accept only WordPress post-safe HTML, including nested JSON/ACF values. Scripts, HTML event handlers, iframe/style tags and executable URLs are refused atomically, even for administrators. Safe core/html content is supported. An untouched stored neighboring block is preserved; do not resend old script-bearing content as a new/replacement block. Theme/plugin code owns interactivity. Use {markup} for blocks whose writeMode is markup. Example: {"markup":"

Hello

"} Preserve attributes encoded in comments, saved HTML and all nested block delimiters. No Markdown-to-block or arbitrary JavaScript save() serializer is provided. Ordinary core blocks are not all attribute-only. Use {name,attributes} only when get-block-source explicitly reports writeMode:"attributes". Never rebuild an entire page merely to update one ACF field. Unknown or unregistered blocks are not new writable blocks; preserve untouched neighboring content rather than silently dropping it. ACF DATA PATCHES ACF data is in attributes.data: field names and _name field-key references, groups with prefixed names, repeaters with a count and row keys such as rows_0_label. Missing field-key references are filled from the registered schema. Read the schema; do not guess field names, keys or choices. Value shapes by field type: text, textarea, wysiwyg, url, email, date -> string. number, range -> number. true_false -> true/false (or 1/0). select, radio, button_group -> the choice's value; checkbox or a multiple select -> a list of values. link -> {"url":"…","title":"…","target":""} (target "_blank" for a new tab). image, file, post_object, user, a single taxonomy -> one id. gallery, relationship, multiple ones -> a list of ids. For op:update only, data is patched by key: omitted fields and rows stay. Example: {"op":"update","index":0,"name":"acf/hero","attributes":{"data":{"headline":"New headline"}}}. Shrinking a repeater removes rows and references beyond the new count. Count 0 clears it; the editor's empty-string count is accepted as zero rows, subject to required/min/max validation. op:replace requires the complete replacement block; it is not a partial data patch. Unknown fields/references, invalid types or failed ACF validation refuse the content save. These checks also apply to nested ACF blocks in supplied markup. Unchanged neighbors are carried without revalidation. usePostMeta, conditional logic, flexible content, clone/custom field types and taxonomy save_terms are unsupported for writes. Respect acf.writable/limitations; do not work around them with raw post meta. CONTENT AND ASSETS Use the existing schema for title, slug, excerpt, featuredImage, parent and menuOrder. Parent must be valid for that type and cannot create a cycle. Title-only updates do not necessarily change a URL. Use set-post-terms for classification. Media belongs to the library; read site-assets-contract. Use synced-pattern-contract for content intentionally shared across pages. Do not insert scripts, event handlers, PHP or remote executable code, and do not use raw HTML to imitate a block the site does not have. The same refusal covers every text a writing tool takes (titles, labels, field values, form templates) and names what it refused ("the onerror attribute on the img element"). Quoting, spacing and "/>" do not matter; "a < b" is plain text, but a "<" right before a letter must be a tag that is closed. To show a tag as words write it with < and >. Inspect the preview and reopen the editor to check block validation before reporting completion. STATUS AND DELETION Use set-content-status to publish, unpublish, trash or restore. delete-content is permanent. The assigned front, posts and not-found pages have protection checks: the site administrator reassigns the front and posts page in Settings first; the not-found page is cleared with update-site-settings. Do not assume deleting a page deletes its attachments or reusable patterns. delete-media is permanent by default and can delete a referenced file: usedBy is informational, not a guarantee of refusal or exhaustive usage detection. Confirm intended deletion and repair known references.
